Container.Name: Nametag
Container.Overview:
Nametag is a personal CRM for the people in your life. Keep notes, birthdays and important dates, see how everyone is connected in an interactive network graph, organize people into groups, keep a journal, and get reminders to stay in touch. Two-way CardDAV sync works with Google Contacts, iCloud, Outlook and Nextcloud.
Before the first start: - Install a PostgreSQL container (for example the official postgres:16 image) and create a database and user for Nametag. - Generate the two secrets in the Unraid terminal with: openssl rand -base64 32 - Run: mkdir -p /mnt/user/appdata/nametag/photos && chown -R 1001:1001 /mnt/user/appdata/nametag (the container runs as UID 1001).
Reminders and CardDAV sync need scheduled calls. The docs linked under Read Me include a ready-to-paste User Scripts entry.
Container.Requires: A PostgreSQL 14+ database (for example the official postgres container). Redis is optional.
Container.ExtraSearchTerms: personal crm contacts relationships birthdays carddav monica

Config.Name: Photos
Config.Description: Where profile photos are stored. Must be owned by UID 1001.

Config.Name: App URL
Config.Description: The address you open Nametag at, for example http://192.168.1.10:3000 or https://nametag.example.com. Used for sign-in and links in emails.

Config.Name: Auth secret
Config.Description: At least 32 characters. Generate with: openssl rand -base64 32

Config.Name: Cron secret
Config.Description: At least 16 characters. Protects the scheduled-job endpoints. Generate with: openssl rand -base64 32

Config.Name: Database host
Config.Description: IP address or container name of your PostgreSQL server.

Config.Name: Database name
Config.Description: Name of the PostgreSQL database. It must already exist.

Config.Name: Disable registration
Config.Description: Set to true after creating your account to stop others from signing up.
